- Model consistently overestimates early in the forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Forecasts tend to peak too high after sharp historical spikes (e.g., 76+), then overshoot and fail to correct downward quickly.
- Mean reversion is underemphasized — model holds high values longer than observed true prices, which often drop sharply after peaks.
- Forecast error is more pronounced in the middle-to-late horizon (days 15–30), suggesting lag or delayed response to market signals.
- Model exhibits persistent upward bias in the first 3–5 days of the forecast, then gradually corrects — but not enough to match true mean reversion.
- Overshoots after spikes are common, especially in the 10–15 day range, where model holds high values while true price corrects downward.
- Model underestimates low-range values (below 65) in the later days, suggesting it fails to recognize downward pressure or supply/demand shifts.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows a tendency to smooth out volatility, underestimating sharp drops and overestimating gradual declines.
